requirements.requirement: Limit datauser to 100 MB under /srv/data using filesystem-native enforcement, with the resulting configuration remaining effective after restart.
requirements.summary: A dedicated XFS filesystem was mounted at /srv/data with user-quota accounting and enforcement enabled. datauser received 100M soft and hard limits. Direct tests before and after restart attempted a 101 MiB write and both stopped at exactly 104,857,600 bytes with “Disk quota exceeded”; cleanup returned usage to zero. The mount, quota state, account, and limits were present after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: The node remained on Red Hat Enterprise Linux 10.0 with kernel 6.12.0-55.9.1.el10_0.x86_64 before and after execution. The implementation used the platform's existing XFS and xfs_quota facilities, and package health remained clean.

overall_summary: Both material task outcomes are satisfied with direct enforcement and post-restart evidence. The mandatory node-restart protocol is coherent: pre-restart boot identity and quota health were captured, restart was acknowledged and observed through connection loss, the post-restart boot identity changed, and system, mount, quota, account, persisted data, and write access recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the restart. Only a minor temporary reboot-log residue detracts from hygiene.
limitations: The lifecycle snapshots are bounded and do not independently inventory the quota mount, account, or fstab entry; those states are instead established by direct executor commands.
The initial discovery command stopped at a missing /srv/data path, but subsequent read-only discovery and the fixed pre-executor platform snapshot provide the missing baseline observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles in creating the filesystem, configuring the quota, verifying enforcement and persistence, performing the mandatory restart, or cleaning test data. The only unnecessary retained mutation was the small /tmp/antrieb-reboot.log file created while scheduling the restart; it remained after execution. No unnecessary reverted mutations were identified. Final observations showed no failed services, no new network exposure, healthy package state, and an empty /srv/data.
